title: Atoms, electrons and charge

concepts.label: charge (+ / −)
concepts.definition: A property of particles that comes in two kinds, positive and negative: opposites attract, likes repel, more strongly the closer they are; electricity is charge that moves.

concepts.label: proton
concepts.definition: A heavy particle in the nucleus with charge +1; protons never move in chemistry.

concepts.label: electron
concepts.definition: A light particle around the nucleus with charge −1; the only particle that atoms exchange, so net charge = protons − electrons.

concepts.label: atomic number Z
concepts.definition: The number of protons in the nucleus; it fixes which element the atom is, and a neutral atom has Z electrons.

concepts.label: electron shell (2, 8, 8)
concepts.definition: Electrons sit in layers around the nucleus that fill from the inside out with 2, 8, 8 seats (a simplified model, valid for Z ≤ 20): Na is 2, 8, 1 and Cl is 2, 8, 7.

concepts.label: valence electron
concepts.definition: An electron in the outermost occupied shell; the only electrons that take part in chemistry.

concepts.label: net pull on the outer shell
concepts.definition: Rough attraction felt by the valence electrons = protons − inner electrons (+1 for Na, +7 for Cl); an informal stand-in for shielding / effective nuclear charge.

concepts.label: full shell (noble-gas configuration)
concepts.definition: An outer shell with every seat taken (2 / 2, 8 / 2, 8, 8, as in He, Ne, Ar): the stable arrangement, expensive to break into and with no seat for an extra electron.

concepts.label: ion
concepts.definition: An atom whose electron count differs from its proton count, so it has a net charge, written as a superscript (Na⁺, Mg²⁺, Cl⁻).

concepts.label: cation (+)
concepts.definition: A positive ion, formed when an atom loses electrons: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻.

concepts.label: anion (−)
concepts.definition: A negative ion, formed when an atom gains electrons: Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻ (named with the ending -ide).

namedOnly: nucleus (used as the place where protons sit)
element (atoms sharing one Z; used, not listed as a concept)
mole / kJ/mol (unit of the cost bars; defined in Ions, salts and electrolytes)
ionisation energy and electron affinity (shown as 'cost to remove' / 'energy released on adding', named in The periodic table)
sharing electrons / covalent bond (Silicon and light)
ionic packing into a salt crystal (Ions, salts and electrolytes)
-ide names: chloride, fluoride, oxide, sulfide, hydride
summary: Running example: sodium (2, 8, 1) and chlorine (2, 8, 7) from a grain of table salt; Na → Na⁺ + e⁻, Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻, then Na + Cl → Na⁺ + Cl⁻ with the ledger 496 kJ/mol paid, 349 returned, the rest covered by the ions attracting. Capstone: an ion workbench for Z = 1–20 where the learner strips or adds electrons and reads real per-electron costs (green valence bars, red full-shell wall), seeing which ions end on a noble-gas configuration cheaply. Hooks for later lessons: 'giver' vs 'taker' atoms, the net pull (+1 … +7) across a row and the cost-of-removal bars (lead into ionisation energy and electronegativity), 'only electrons move', charge is conserved, and 'route the electron through a wire and you have a current'.
